note: Bad claims planted in follow-up sentences, six types with five each, written and labeled before the checker was scored on them. Each is judged against the call's answer key. It counts as caught when the checker flags a claim that overlaps the bad words, and the right call when the status matches too. Swapped claims use a real number or date from the call on the wrong thing.

claims.sentence: You lost about $15,000 of seafood and dairy in that one load.
The hardware comes to about $35,000 for the 38 trucks and the warehouse.
We can fit everything into about $800 a month.
claims.truth: The budget was about $500 a month (s07f11).

claims.sentence: That one load cost you about $5,000 in seafood and dairy.
claims.truth: $5,000 was the monthly credits. The load was $14,000 (d1f02).

claims.sentence: Anything over $20,000 goes to the partners' monthly meeting.
claims.truth: $20,000 was the upgrade budget. The partners take anything over $15,000 (s09f07).

claims.sentence: A quote for your fourteen vans and the walk-in is on its way.
The proposal covers all eight cold rooms.
Priya's pilot plan covers six trucks on real routes.
The telematics add-on only reports every ten minutes.
claims.truth: Ten minutes was the alert target. The add-on reports every thirty (s05f05).

claims.sentence: Three restaurants ran out of prep and cut half the brunch menu.
claims.truth: Two restaurants (s03f03). Three was the truck count.

claims.sentence: Frostgauge's hardware came in about 40% cheaper.
Their quote came in about 20% under ours.
Refunds on warm boxes hit about 5% of boxes this summer.
If the alerts catch 80% of last year's losses they cover year one.
About 30% of your routes cross dead zones.
claims.truth: Half the routes (d2f05). 30% was the Frostgauge price gap.

claims.sentence: Priya and I will see you and Tom next Wednesday at ten.
You'll have the proposal and the insurance certificate by Monday.
The demo for Kim is set for next Tuesday at nine.
Linda will make the call by October 2.
claims.truth: Linda decides by Wednesday the 30th (d3f26). October 2 is the signature.

claims.sentence: Priya will send the written pilot plan by Friday.
claims.truth: By Thursday (d2f15). Friday is Tom's questionnaire.

claims.sentence: We'll bring Kevin from our install team to the technical call.
claims.truth: Nobody named Kevin is on the call or mentioned in it.

claims.sentence: Tom, your CFO, signs off on anything over $25,000.
claims.truth: Tom is the IT manager, and Linda is the CFO.

claims.sentence: I'll send Priya the vendor registration information this week.
claims.truth: Priya is from the deal, not this call.

claims.sentence: Rachel, your CFO, will get the proposal to counsel the day it arrives.
claims.truth: Rachel is the director of operations.

claims.sentence: Angela will take it to Susan Park herself.
claims.truth: Angela takes it to Mark Feldman (s01f10).

claims.sentence: As we discussed we'll waive the installation.
claims.truth: Marcus floated it (d3k02), and nobody has approved it.

claims.sentence: The installation is on us at no cost.
We'll take 10% off the hardware if you sign this month.
We guarantee the alerts will pay for themselves in the first season.
The first month of software is free.
